ID_8.lede: Nine PMS2 pseudogene copies strung across chr7 — every one recovered. A tenth PMS2 copy was discovered off Soto's catalogue: it's homologous to a PMS2 member (not to its physical neighbour), the case that motivated attributing candidates by homology rather than proximity.

discoveries.note: 75 reads, 97.9% identical to a PMS2 member, 13.8 kb (1.2× the family's typical member). A genuine new PMS2 copy. Its nearest catalogued neighbour is a SPDYE gene, so a proximity rule would mislabel it — homology puts it here correctly.

ID_131.lede: The amylase copy-number locus. Five of six annotated copies recover cleanly; the single miss is a 199 bp fragment — too short to carry a distinguishing read. Two well-expressed new amylase copies were discovered in the gap.

discoveries.note: 23 reads, 98.0% to AMYP1, but 24.7 kb — 2.9× the family's median member. A size outlier: possibly a chimeric or extended span rather than a clean amylase copy. Worth a look before crediting it.
146 reads, 99.3% to AMY1A, 7.8 kb (0.9× the family's members) — a clean new amylase copy.

members.why: 199 bp fragment — too short for a distinguishing read

ID_402.lede: Three NCF1 copies, each with reads — 15, 44, 17. But they are exon-identical: every read ties across all three at MAPQ 0, so not one can be assigned to a specific copy. This is the identifiability floor — expression is present, resolution is not, and DNA is required.

members.why: reads absorbed by a sibling copy
